subject: medicine
stem: A 32-year-old man with a family history of sudden cardiac death has a non-diagnostic resting ECG. Which drug is used as a provocation test to unmask a type 1 Brugada pattern?
reason: Sodium channel blockers (ajmaline, flecainide, procainamide) unmask the coved ST elevation.
explanation: Brugada syndrome is most often due to loss of function in the cardiac sodium channel (SCN5A). Sodium channel blockers exaggerate the defect and bring out coved ST elevation of 2 mm or more in V1 to V2. Isoprenaline and quinidine do the opposite and are used to treat electrical storm.
pearl: Placing V1 and V2 in the 2nd or 3rd intercostal space increases the sensitivity of the ECG.

subject: medicine
stem: The autoantibody found in about 70% of adults with primary membranous nephropathy is directed against:
options: Alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen
reason: Anti-PLA2R is the dominant antibody in primary membranous nephropathy.
explanation: PLA2R on the podocyte is the target in roughly 70% of primary membranous nephropathy. THSD7A accounts for a small percentage and has an association with malignancy. Anti-nephrin antibodies are linked to minimal change disease. The alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen is the target in anti-GBM disease.
pearl: Falling anti-PLA2R titres predict remission before proteinuria improves.

subject: medicine
stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with new psychosis, orofacial dyskinesias, seizures and autonomic instability. CSF is positive for anti-NMDA receptor antibodies. Which tumour should be looked for?
reason: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis in young women is classically linked to ovarian teratoma.
explanation: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis typically starts with psychiatric features, then movement disorder, seizures, autonomic instability and hypoventilation. In young women an ovarian teratoma is found in a substantial proportion, and removing it improves outcome alongside immunotherapy.
pearl: EEG may show the extreme delta brush pattern.

subject: medicine
stem: A 42-year-old with confirmed primary aldosteronism has a 1.2 cm left adrenal nodule on CT and wants surgery. Which test best distinguishes unilateral from bilateral disease before adrenalectomy?
reason: CT alone misclassifies many patients; adrenal venous sampling lateralises the source.
explanation: The aldosterone-to-renin ratio is the screening test and saline infusion is a confirmatory test. Neither tells which side is responsible. CT can show a non-functioning incidentaloma or miss a small adenoma, so adrenal venous sampling is the reference test for lateralisation before surgery.
pearl: It may be skipped in patients under 35 with marked disease and a clear unilateral adenoma on CT.

subject: medicine
stem: Clinically significant portal hypertension is defined by a hepatic venous pressure gradient of:
reason: 10 mmHg or more is the threshold at which varices and decompensation can develop.
explanation: Normal gradient is 1 to 5 mmHg, and more than 5 mmHg is portal hypertension. At 10 mmHg or more it is clinically significant. At 12 mmHg or more variceal bleeding can occur. A gradient of 20 mmHg or more in acute variceal bleeding predicts treatment failure.
pearl: Non-selective beta blockers aim to lower the gradient below 12 mmHg or by at least 20% from baseline.

subject: medicine
stem: According to the 2022 ESC/ERS guidelines, pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension is defined haemodynamically as:
reason: 2022 update: mPAP above 20 mmHg, wedge 15 or less, PVR above 2 Wood units.
explanation: The 2022 guidelines lowered the mean pulmonary artery pressure cut-off from 25 to above 20 mmHg and the pulmonary vascular resistance cut-off from 3 to above 2 Wood units. A wedge pressure of 15 mmHg or less marks pre-capillary disease; above 15 marks post-capillary disease.
pearl: Right heart catheterisation is mandatory for diagnosis; echocardiography only estimates probability.

subject: medicine
stem: A 30-year-old woman has fever, confusion, platelets of 18,000 per microlitre, schistocytes on smear, raised LDH and normal PT and aPTT. What is the most important immediate treatment?
reason: This is TTP; plasma exchange is life-saving and should not wait for the ADAMTS13 result.
explanation: Microangiopathic haemolysis with severe thrombocytopenia, neurological signs and a normal coagulation profile points to thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Plasma exchange removes the anti-ADAMTS13 antibody and replaces the enzyme. Steroids are added, and caplacizumab and rituximab are used where available.
pearl: ADAMTS13 activity below 10% confirms the diagnosis. Avoid platelet transfusion unless there is life-threatening bleeding.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with a heliotrope rash, Gottron papules and no muscle weakness develops rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease. Which antibody is most likely to be positive?
reason: Anti-MDA5: clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive lung disease.
explanation: Anti-MDA5 marks clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis with skin ulceration and a high risk of rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease. Anti-Mi-2 goes with classic dermatomyositis and a good response to treatment. Anti-TIF1 gamma is linked to malignancy in adults. Anti-SRP goes with necrotising myopathy.
pearl: A very high ferritin in anti-MDA5 disease signals a worse prognosis.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction is being switched from enalapril to sacubitril-valsartan. What is the minimum gap needed after the last enalapril dose?
reason: A 36-hour washout lowers the risk of angioedema.
explanation: Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin, which breaks down bradykinin. ACE inhibitors also raise bradykinin, so overlapping the two sharply increases the risk of angioedema. A 36-hour gap is required after stopping an ACE inhibitor. No washout is needed when switching from an ARB.
pearl: BNP rises on sacubitril-valsartan; use NT-proBNP for monitoring.

subject: medicine
stem: A treatment-naive patient with HIV and a CD4 count of 40 is diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis and started on antifungal induction. When should antiretroviral therapy be started?
reason: Early ART in cryptococcal meningitis increases mortality from IRIS.
explanation: Starting antiretroviral therapy early in cryptococcal meningitis increases deaths, largely through immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome inside the closed cranial space. WHO recommends deferring it for 4 to 6 weeks after starting antifungal treatment.
pearl: Raised intracranial pressure is managed with repeated therapeutic lumbar punctures, not acetazolamide or steroids.

subject: medicine
stem: A 58-year-old presents to a rural hospital 2 hours after onset of chest pain with anterior ST elevation. The nearest PCI centre is 3 hours away. What is the best reperfusion strategy?
options: Fibrinolysis only if pain persists at 6 hours
reason: If PCI cannot be delivered within 120 minutes, give fibrinolysis without delay.
explanation: Primary PCI is preferred when it can be performed within 120 minutes of diagnosis. Otherwise fibrinolysis is given immediately, ideally within 10 minutes, followed by transfer for angiography 2 to 24 hours later. This is the pharmaco-invasive strategy.
pearl: Failed fibrinolysis (less than 50% ST resolution at 60 to 90 minutes) needs rescue PCI.

subject: medicine
stem: A 72-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes is found to have atrial fibrillation. She has no history of stroke, heart failure or vascular disease. What is her CHA2DS2-VASc score?
reason: Age 65 to 74 (1) + female (1) + hypertension (1) + diabetes (1) = 4.
explanation: The score gives 1 point each for heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, vascular disease, age 65 to 74 and female sex, and 2 points each for age 75 or more and prior stroke or TIA. She scores 4 and should receive oral anticoagulation, preferably a DOAC.
pearl: Female sex alone, with no other risk factor, does not justify anticoagulation.

subject: medicine
stem: Mavacamten, used in symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, acts by:
reason: It is a selective cardiac myosin inhibitor that reduces hypercontractility.
explanation: Mavacamten reduces the number of myosin heads that can bind actin, lowering contractility and the outflow tract gradient. It improved symptoms and exercise capacity in the EXPLORER-HCM trial. Ejection fraction must be monitored because it can cause systolic dysfunction.
pearl: Avoid vasodilators and high-dose diuretics in obstructive HCM; they worsen the gradient.

subject: medicine
stem: Which set of echocardiographic values defines severe aortic stenosis?
options: Peak velocity 5 m/s, mean gradient 20 mmHg, area 1.8 cm2
Peak velocity 3 m/s, mean gradient 25 mmHg, area 1.5 cm2
Peak velocity 4 m/s or more, mean gradient 40 mmHg or more, area under 1 cm2
Peak velocity 2.5 m/s, mean gradient 15 mmHg, area 2 cm2
reason: Severe: velocity 4 m/s or more, mean gradient 40 mmHg or more, area below 1 cm2.
explanation: These three values define high-gradient severe aortic stenosis. When the area is below 1 cm2 but the gradient is low, low-flow low-gradient stenosis is considered and dobutamine stress echocardiography or CT calcium scoring is used to confirm severity.
pearl: Symptoms (angina, syncope, dyspnoea) or an ejection fraction below 50% indicate valve replacement.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with Staphylococcus aureus aortic valve endocarditis develops a PR interval that lengthens progressively to complete heart block. What does this indicate?
reason: New conduction block in aortic endocarditis means extension into the root.
explanation: The conduction system runs close to the aortic root. A new atrioventricular block signals perivalvular extension or abscess, which represents uncontrolled infection and is an indication for urgent surgery. Transoesophageal echocardiography is the investigation of choice.
pearl: The three surgical indications are heart failure, uncontrolled infection and prevention of embolism.

subject: medicine
stem: A woman on erythromycin and ondansetron has recurrent syncope. The monitor shows polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with a twisting axis and she has a pulse. What is the first-line drug?
reason: Torsades de pointes: magnesium 2 g IV, even if serum magnesium is normal.
explanation: Torsades de pointes arises on a prolonged QT interval. Magnesium suppresses the early afterdepolarisations that trigger it. Offending drugs are stopped and potassium is corrected. Amiodarone and procainamide prolong the QT further and are avoided.
pearl: Refractory cases are treated by raising the heart rate with pacing or isoprenaline.

subject: medicine
stem: A 76-year-old man has heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, thick ventricular walls and low ECG voltages. Serum and urine show no monoclonal protein. Which test can confirm the diagnosis without biopsy?
reason: Grade 2 to 3 cardiac uptake with no monoclonal protein confirms ATTR amyloidosis.
explanation: Transthyretin amyloid takes up bone-seeking tracers. Grade 2 or 3 myocardial uptake, once light-chain amyloidosis has been excluded by serum free light chains and serum and urine immunofixation, is diagnostic of ATTR cardiomyopathy. Tafamidis stabilises the transthyretin tetramer.
pearl: Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome and lumbar canal stenosis often precede the cardiac disease by years.

subject: medicine
stem: A normotensive patient with acute pulmonary embolism has right ventricular dilatation on echocardiography and a raised troponin. What is the recommended initial management?
reason: Intermediate-high risk: anticoagulate and monitor; thrombolyse only on deterioration.
explanation: Systemic thrombolysis is reserved for high-risk pulmonary embolism with shock or persistent hypotension. In intermediate-high risk patients the PEITHO trial showed that routine thrombolysis prevented decompensation but caused more major bleeding and stroke, so rescue reperfusion is used if they deteriorate.
pearl: Low molecular weight heparin is preferred over unfractionated heparin unless reperfusion is likely.

subject: medicine
stem: Avacopan, used as a steroid-sparing agent in ANCA-associated vasculitis, acts by:
reason: Avacopan is an oral C5a receptor antagonist.
explanation: The alternative complement pathway and C5a amplify neutrophil activation in ANCA-associated vasculitis. In the ADVOCATE trial, avacopan in place of a prednisolone taper was non-inferior for remission at 26 weeks and superior for sustained remission at 52 weeks.
pearl: Induction still requires rituximab or cyclophosphamide alongside it.

subject: medicine
stem: A 60-year-old has a generalised seizure. Serum sodium is 108 mmol/L. What is the correct immediate treatment?
reason: Severe symptoms: bolus hypertonic saline to raise sodium by about 5 mmol/L.
explanation: Seizures or coma from hyponatraemia are treated with boluses of 3% saline, repeated if needed, aiming for a rise of 4 to 6 mmol/L in the first hours. Total correction should not exceed 8 to 10 mmol/L in 24 hours, to avoid osmotic demyelination.
pearl: Alcoholism, malnutrition and hypokalaemia increase the risk of osmotic demyelination.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with potassium of 7.2 mmol/L has widened QRS complexes on ECG. Which is the first drug to give?
reason: Calcium stabilises the myocardium within minutes; it does not lower potassium.
explanation: ECG changes mean the membrane must be stabilised first with intravenous calcium. Insulin with dextrose and salbutamol then shift potassium into cells. Removal from the body needs diuretics, potassium binders or dialysis.
pearl: The effect of calcium lasts only 30 to 60 minutes; repeat if ECG changes persist.

subject: medicine
stem: A diabetic man with mild CKD has potassium 5.9 mmol/L, bicarbonate 17 mmol/L, a normal anion gap and urine pH of 5.0. What is the most likely diagnosis?
reason: Hyperkalaemia with normal anion gap acidosis and acid urine = type 4.
explanation: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis results from hyporeninaemic hypoaldosteronism, common in diabetic nephropathy. Hyperkalaemia suppresses ammonia production, but the urine can still be acidified. Types 1 and 2 cause hypokalaemia, and in type 1 the urine pH stays above 5.5.
pearl: ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs, heparin and trimethoprim can unmask or worsen it.

subject: medicine
stem: The early fall in eGFR and the long-term renal protection seen with SGLT2 inhibitors are best explained by:
options: Afferent arteriolar constriction via tubuloglomerular feedback
Reduced renin release from the macula densa
reason: More sodium at the macula densa restores feedback and lowers glomerular pressure.
explanation: Blocking proximal sodium-glucose reabsorption increases sodium chloride delivery to the macula densa. Tubuloglomerular feedback constricts the afferent arteriole and reduces intraglomerular pressure and hyperfiltration. The small initial fall in eGFR is haemodynamic and reversible.
pearl: The benefit is seen in CKD with and without diabetes.

subject: medicine
stem: A 25-year-old man has haemoptysis and rapidly progressive renal failure. Biopsy shows crescents with linear IgG along the glomerular basement membrane. What is the treatment?
reason: Anti-GBM disease: remove the antibody and stop its production.
explanation: Anti-GBM disease is caused by antibodies against the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen. Plasma exchange removes circulating antibody quickly while cyclophosphamide and steroids suppress production. Outcome depends on renal function at presentation.
pearl: Dialysis dependence with 100% crescents at presentation predicts little chance of renal recovery.

subject: medicine
stem: A 66-year-old was last seen well 10 hours ago and has an NIHSS of 16. CT angiography shows a proximal middle cerebral artery occlusion, and perfusion imaging shows a small core with a large penumbra. What is the best treatment?
options: Aspirin and admit to stroke unit
reason: Large vessel occlusion with mismatch: thrombectomy up to 24 hours.
explanation: Intravenous thrombolysis is limited to 4.5 hours in standard practice. The DAWN and DEFUSE-3 trials showed that thrombectomy benefits selected patients with anterior large vessel occlusion and a favourable core to penumbra mismatch between 6 and 24 hours.
pearl: Selection in the late window is by tissue, not by the clock.

subject: medicine
stem: Which statement about MuSK antibody-positive myasthenia gravis is correct?
options: Thymoma is found in most patients
Bulbar weakness is prominent and rituximab is effective
reason: MuSK myasthenia: bulbar, facial and neck weakness, with a good response to rituximab.
explanation: MuSK antibodies are IgG4 and are found in a proportion of patients who lack acetylcholine receptor antibodies. Weakness is predominantly bulbar, facial and respiratory. Response to pyridostigmine is often poor, thymic pathology is absent and thymectomy has no proven benefit.
pearl: Plasma exchange works better than IVIG in a MuSK crisis.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with Guillain-Barre syndrome can no longer walk unaided. Which treatment has been shown to be of no benefit?
reason: Steroids do not help in Guillain-Barre syndrome.
explanation: Intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange are equally effective when started early, and combining them adds nothing. Trials of oral and intravenous corticosteroids showed no benefit. Monitoring of vital capacity and autonomic function is essential.
pearl: Intubate when vital capacity falls below about 20 mL/kg.

subject: medicine
stem: A 35-year-old woman has intractable hiccups and vomiting for 3 weeks, followed by paraparesis. MRI shows a spinal cord lesion spanning five vertebral segments. Which antibody should be tested?
reason: Area postrema syndrome plus longitudinally extensive myelitis = NMOSD.
explanation: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder is an astrocytopathy caused by aquaporin-4 IgG. Core features are optic neuritis, myelitis extending over three or more vertebral segments, and area postrema syndrome. Relapses are prevented with agents such as rituximab, eculizumab, inebilizumab or satralizumab.
pearl: Some multiple sclerosis drugs, including interferon beta and natalizumab, can worsen NMOSD.

subject: medicine
stem: A 19-year-old has tremor, dysarthria and deranged liver enzymes. MRI of the midbrain shows the 'face of the giant panda' sign. What is the diagnosis?
reason: The panda sign in a young patient with liver and movement problems is Wilson disease.
explanation: Wilson disease is due to ATP7B mutations that impair biliary copper excretion. Diagnosis rests on low ceruloplasmin, raised 24-hour urinary copper and Kayser-Fleischer rings, which are almost always present when there is neurological disease. Treatment is chelation or zinc.
pearl: Neurological symptoms can worsen at the start of penicillamine.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient is still convulsing after two adequate doses of intravenous lorazepam. Based on the ESETT trial, which statement about the next drug is correct?
options: Phenobarbital must always be used second
Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate are equally effective
Valproate is contraindicated in status epilepticus
Fosphenytoin is superior to the others
reason: ESETT: all three stop seizures in about half of patients.
explanation: In benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus, the ESETT trial found no difference in efficacy or safety between levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate. The choice depends on comorbidity: avoid valproate in pregnancy and liver disease, and fosphenytoin in cardiac conduction disease.
pearl: If the second-line drug fails, proceed to anaesthetic infusion with EEG monitoring.

subject: medicine
stem: A 35-year-old man has attacks of severe unilateral orbital pain lasting 45 minutes with lacrimation and nasal congestion, occurring nightly for 3 weeks. What is the best acute treatment?
reason: Cluster headache: oxygen at 12 to 15 L/min or subcutaneous sumatriptan.
explanation: Cluster headache is a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia with short, severe, strictly unilateral attacks and restlessness. Attacks are aborted with high-flow oxygen through a non-rebreathing mask or subcutaneous sumatriptan. Verapamil is the main preventive drug.
pearl: A short course of steroids bridges the gap until verapamil takes effect.

subject: medicine
stem: A woman has confirmed ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome. Pituitary MRI is normal. What is the next investigation?
reason: Petrosal sinus sampling separates pituitary from ectopic ACTH.
explanation: Many corticotroph adenomas are too small to see on MRI. A central-to-peripheral ACTH ratio of 2 or more at baseline, or 3 or more after CRH or desmopressin stimulation, confirms a pituitary source. It localises the source to the pituitary but lateralises poorly.
pearl: Lesions under 6 mm on MRI may be incidental, so sampling is still advised.

subject: medicine
stem: A 40-year-old has enlarging hands, coarse facial features and new diabetes. What is the best initial screening test?
reason: IGF-1 is stable through the day and reflects integrated growth hormone secretion.
explanation: Growth hormone is secreted in pulses, so a random level is unreliable. A raised age-adjusted IGF-1 is the screening test. Confirmation is failure of growth hormone to suppress during an oral glucose tolerance test, followed by MRI of the pituitary.
pearl: Screen for colonic polyps, sleep apnoea and cardiomyopathy once the diagnosis is made.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis has pH 7.05, glucose 520 mg/dL and potassium 3.0 mmol/L. After starting saline, what is the next step?
options: Replace potassium and withhold insulin until it is above 3.3
reason: Insulin drives potassium into cells; starting it at 3.0 risks fatal arrhythmia.
explanation: Total body potassium is depleted in ketoacidosis even when the serum level looks normal. If potassium is below 3.3 mmol/L, insulin is withheld and potassium replaced first. Between 3.3 and 5.3 mmol/L, potassium is added to each litre of fluid.
pearl: Bicarbonate is considered only when pH is below 6.9.

subject: medicine
stem: In thyroid storm, why is iodine given at least one hour after the thionamide?
options: To allow propranolol to act first
So that iodine is not used as substrate for new hormone
reason: Block synthesis first, then give iodine to block release.
explanation: A thionamide blocks organification, so iodine given afterwards cannot be built into new hormone and instead inhibits hormone release (Wolff-Chaikoff effect). Propylthiouracil is preferred because it also reduces T4 to T3 conversion. Beta blockade and steroids complete the regimen.
pearl: The Burch-Wartofsky score helps identify storm; 45 or more is highly suggestive.

subject: medicine
stem: A man with squamous cell lung cancer has calcium of 14.5 mg/dL, suppressed PTH and low 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D. What is the mechanism?
reason: Humoral hypercalcaemia of malignancy is mediated by PTHrP.
explanation: PTH-related peptide acts on the PTH receptor to increase bone resorption and renal calcium reabsorption, but unlike PTH it does not raise 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D. It is typical of squamous cancers. Lymphomas cause hypercalcaemia through excess 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.
pearl: Treatment is intravenous saline followed by zoledronate; denosumab if refractory.

subject: medicine
stem: A slim 22-year-old has fasting glucose persistently around 118 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.3%. Her father and grandfather have the same mild pattern without complications. Antibodies are negative. What is the management?
reason: GCK-MODY: a reset glucose set-point that needs no treatment.
explanation: Glucokinase mutations raise the threshold for insulin secretion, giving mild, stable fasting hyperglycaemia from birth. Complications are rare and treatment does not change the glucose level. HNF1A-MODY, by contrast, is progressive and very sensitive to low-dose sulfonylureas.
pearl: Pregnancy is the one setting where GCK-MODY may need management, guided by fetal growth.

subject: medicine
stem: A woman with known Addison disease presents with vomiting, blood pressure 76/40 mmHg and sodium 124 mmol/L. What is the immediate treatment?
options: Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV and rapid saline
Await a cortisol result before treating
reason: Adrenal crisis: treat at once with hydrocortisone and saline.
explanation: Adrenal crisis is a clinical diagnosis and treatment is never delayed for tests. Hydrocortisone 100 mg is given intravenously, followed by 200 mg over 24 hours, with rapid 0.9% saline. At these doses hydrocortisone provides enough mineralocorticoid effect.
pearl: Teach sick-day rules: double or triple the dose during illness and carry injectable hydrocortisone.

subject: medicine
stem: In a patient already on a gluten-free diet, which test has the highest negative predictive value for excluding coeliac disease?
reason: Without DQ2 or DQ8, coeliac disease is essentially excluded.
explanation: Serology and histology become normal on a gluten-free diet and cannot exclude the disease. Nearly all patients carry HLA-DQ2 or DQ8, so their absence rules it out. Their presence is common in the general population and does not confirm the diagnosis.
pearl: Always check total IgA with tTG-IgA; IgA deficiency gives a false negative.

subject: medicine
stem: In acute liver failure due to paracetamol, which finding alone meets the King's College criteria for transplantation?
options: Arterial pH below 7.30 after fluid resuscitation
reason: Persisting acidosis after resuscitation is a stand-alone criterion.
explanation: For paracetamol, the criteria are arterial pH below 7.30 after resuscitation, or all three of INR above 6.5, creatinine above 3.4 mg/dL and grade III to IV encephalopathy. Bilirubin and age belong to the non-paracetamol criteria. The height of ALT has no prognostic value.
pearl: A raised arterial lactate after resuscitation adds to the sensitivity of the criteria.

subject: medicine
stem: A 45-year-old has HBsAg positive, HBeAg negative, anti-HBe positive, HBV DNA 2 million IU/mL and ALT three times normal. What explains this pattern?
options: Precore or basal core promoter mutant infection
reason: Active hepatitis without HBeAg: the virus cannot make e antigen.
explanation: Precore and basal core promoter mutations stop or reduce HBeAg production while viral replication continues. This is HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B, with high DNA and fluctuating ALT. An inactive carrier has low DNA and persistently normal ALT.
pearl: Treatment is long-term entecavir or tenofovir.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with Child-Pugh C cirrhosis (score 11) has variceal bleeding controlled by terlipressin and band ligation. What should be offered next to improve survival?
reason: High-risk patients benefit from early TIPS after the bleeding is controlled.
explanation: Pre-emptive TIPS within 72 hours, ideally 24, reduces rebleeding and mortality in Child-Pugh C patients with a score below 14 and in Child-Pugh B patients above 7 with active bleeding at endoscopy. Others receive beta blockers with repeat band ligation.
pearl: Prophylactic antibiotics such as ceftriaxone are given to every cirrhotic with a variceal bleed.

subject: medicine
stem: Ascitic fluid in a cirrhotic patient with fever shows 480 neutrophils per mm3. Besides cefotaxime, which measure reduces hepatorenal syndrome and mortality?
options: Intravenous albumin on day 1 and day 3
reason: Albumin 1.5 g/kg on day 1 and 1 g/kg on day 3.
explanation: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is diagnosed when ascitic neutrophils reach 250 per mm3 or more. Infection worsens circulatory dysfunction and often precipitates hepatorenal syndrome. Albumin with antibiotics reduces renal failure and death, most clearly in those with raised bilirubin or creatinine.
pearl: After one episode, long-term antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated.

subject: medicine
stem: A 28-year-old man with asthma has repeated food bolus impaction. Endoscopy shows rings and linear furrows. What biopsy finding confirms the diagnosis?
options: At least 15 eosinophils per high-power field
reason: Eosinophilic oesophagitis: 15 or more eosinophils per high-power field.
explanation: Eosinophilic oesophagitis is a chronic allergen-driven disease seen in atopic young men. Biopsies are taken from both proximal and distal oesophagus. Treatment options are proton pump inhibitors, swallowed topical steroids, elimination diets and dupilumab, with dilatation for strictures.
pearl: It is the commonest cause of food bolus impaction in young adults.

subject: medicine
stem: Vedolizumab, used in ulcerative colitis and Crohn disease, acts by blocking:
options: The p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23
reason: It blocks gut homing of lymphocytes through alpha-4 beta-7.
explanation: Alpha-4 beta-7 integrin on lymphocytes binds MAdCAM-1 on gut endothelium. Blocking it gives gut-selective immunosuppression. Ustekinumab targets the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23, and tofacitinib and upadacitinib are Janus kinase inhibitors.
pearl: Natalizumab blocks alpha-4 more broadly, which explains its risk of PML.

subject: medicine
stem: A ventilated patient with ARDS has a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of 110 on PEEP 12 and tidal volume 6 mL/kg. Which intervention has been shown to reduce mortality?
options: Prone positioning for at least 16 hours a day
reason: PROSEVA: early prolonged proning in moderate to severe ARDS saves lives.
explanation: In patients with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio below 150, prone sessions of at least 16 hours a day reduced 28-day mortality in the PROSEVA trial. Low tidal volume ventilation is the other proven intervention. Nitric oxide improves oxygenation without improving survival.
pearl: Berlin severity: mild 200 to 300, moderate 100 to 200, severe below 100.

subject: medicine
stem: A 68-year-old has idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with a UIP pattern on CT. Which treatment was shown to increase death and hospitalisation?
reason: PANTHER-IPF: triple immunosuppression causes harm.
explanation: The PANTHER trial was stopped early because the combination of prednisolone, azathioprine and N-acetylcysteine increased mortality and admissions. The antifibrotics nintedanib and pirfenidone slow the decline in forced vital capacity. Lung transplantation is the only treatment that prolongs survival substantially.
pearl: A definite UIP pattern on CT in the right clinical setting does not need a biopsy.

subject: medicine
stem: Tezepelumab, a biologic for severe asthma that works irrespective of eosinophil count, targets:
reason: It blocks TSLP, an epithelial alarmin at the top of the inflammatory cascade.
explanation: TSLP is released by airway epithelium and drives both type 2 and non-type 2 inflammation, which is why tezepelumab works across phenotypes. Mepolizumab and reslizumab block IL-5, benralizumab its receptor, omalizumab IgE, and dupilumab the IL-4 receptor alpha chain.
pearl: Dupilumab can cause a transient rise in blood eosinophils.

subject: medicine
stem: A 30-year-old woman has fever, erythema nodosum, bilateral ankle arthritis and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest X-ray. What is the appropriate approach?
reason: Lofgren syndrome is diagnosed clinically and usually resolves by itself.
explanation: The combination of erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, arthritis and fever is highly specific for acute sarcoidosis. Biopsy is not needed in a typical case. Most patients remit within months to 2 years with symptomatic treatment alone.
pearl: Heerfordt syndrome is uveitis, parotid enlargement, facial palsy and fever.

subject: medicine
stem: A stable patient with COPD has resting PaO2 of 52 mmHg on room air on two occasions 3 weeks apart. Which intervention improves survival?
options: Long-term oxygen for at least 15 hours a day
reason: Long-term oxygen improves survival when resting PaO2 is 55 mmHg or less.
explanation: Long-term oxygen is indicated for a resting PaO2 of 55 mmHg or less or saturation of 88% or less, or a PaO2 of 56 to 59 mmHg with cor pulmonale or polycythaemia. Benefit requires at least 15 hours of use a day. Smoking cessation is the other intervention that prolongs life.
pearl: Oxygen for moderate or exertion-only desaturation showed no survival benefit in the LOTT trial.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with chronic myeloid leukaemia loses response to imatinib and then dasatinib. Mutation analysis shows T315I. Which drug is appropriate?
reason: T315I confers resistance to all earlier tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
explanation: The T315I gatekeeper mutation blocks binding of imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib and bosutinib. Ponatinib was designed to overcome it, and asciminib, which binds the myristoyl pocket, is also active at a higher dose. Allogeneic transplantation is considered in eligible patients.
pearl: Ponatinib carries a risk of arterial occlusive events; control cardiovascular risk factors.

subject: medicine
stem: A 30-year-old has gum bleeding, fibrinogen of 80 mg/dL, and promyelocytes with multiple Auer rods on the smear. What should be done first?
reason: Suspected APL: start ATRA at once, before genetic confirmation.
explanation: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia carries a high risk of early death from haemorrhage. All-trans retinoic acid is started on morphological suspicion, with aggressive correction of fibrinogen and platelets. Confirmation of t(15;17) PML-RARA follows. Arsenic trioxide is added for definitive treatment.
pearl: Differentiation syndrome (fever, weight gain, lung infiltrates) is treated with dexamethasone.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with 30% clonal marrow plasma cells has no hypercalcaemia, renal failure, anaemia or bone lesions. Which finding still makes the diagnosis active multiple myeloma?
options: Involved to uninvolved free light chain ratio of 100 or more
Bence Jones proteinuria of 300 mg per day
reason: A light chain ratio of 100 or more is a myeloma-defining event.
explanation: The SLiM criteria define myeloma needing treatment even without CRAB features: 60% or more clonal plasma cells, an involved to uninvolved serum free light chain ratio of 100 or more, or more than one focal lesion of at least 5 mm on MRI.
pearl: Without these, the same patient has smouldering myeloma.

subject: medicine
stem: Seven days after starting unfractionated heparin a patient's platelets fall from 240,000 to 90,000 and a new deep vein thrombosis appears. What is the correct management?
options: Switch to low molecular weight heparin
reason: HIT: stop all heparin and give a non-heparin anticoagulant.
explanation: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is caused by antibodies to platelet factor 4-heparin complexes and is strongly prothrombotic. All heparin, including flushes and low molecular weight heparin, is stopped. Argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC is used. Warfarin is deferred until platelets recover.
pearl: Starting warfarin early can cause venous limb gangrene through protein C depletion.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient with haemolysis, pancytopenia and hepatic vein thrombosis has loss of CD55 and CD59 on flow cytometry. Before starting eculizumab, what is mandatory?
reason: Blocking C5 removes the defence against Neisseria.
explanation: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria results from PIGA mutation and loss of GPI-anchored complement regulators. Eculizumab and ravulizumab block C5 and prevent intravascular haemolysis and thrombosis. Terminal complement blockade greatly increases the risk of meningococcal infection.
pearl: Thrombosis at unusual sites is the leading cause of death in untreated disease.

subject: medicine
stem: Emicizumab prevents bleeding in haemophilia A, including patients with inhibitors, by:
options: Bridging factors IXa and X as a bispecific antibody
Replacing factor VIII by gene transfer
reason: It mimics the cofactor function of factor VIIIa.
explanation: Emicizumab is a bispecific antibody that brings activated factor IX and factor X together, replacing the function of factor VIIIa. It is not recognised by factor VIII inhibitors and is given subcutaneously. Fitusiran lowers antithrombin and concizumab blocks tissue factor pathway inhibitor.
pearl: It interferes with aPTT-based assays; use chromogenic assays with bovine reagents.

subject: medicine
stem: A 34-year-old woman with antiphospholipid syndrome is positive for lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I. She has had an ischaemic stroke. Which long-term anticoagulant is recommended?
reason: Triple-positive or arterial antiphospholipid syndrome: warfarin, not a DOAC.
explanation: The TRAPS trial of rivaroxaban against warfarin in triple-positive patients was stopped early because of excess arterial thrombosis with rivaroxaban. Vitamin K antagonists remain the standard for high-risk antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly with arterial events.
pearl: Diagnosis needs persistent antibodies on two tests at least 12 weeks apart.

subject: medicine
stem: A 74-year-old has new temporal headache, jaw claudication and transient loss of vision in one eye. ESR is 96 mm/h. What is the immediate step?
reason: Visual symptoms: steroids now, biopsy later.
explanation: Giant cell arteritis can cause irreversible blindness from anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy. Treatment must not wait for biopsy, which stays positive for at least 1 to 2 weeks after starting steroids. Patients with visual symptoms are usually given intravenous methylprednisolone.
pearl: Tocilizumab is an effective steroid-sparing agent.

subject: medicine
stem: Before starting allopurinol in a patient of Han Chinese or Thai ancestry, which test reduces the risk of severe cutaneous adverse reactions?
reason: HLA-B*58:01 carriers are at high risk of allopurinol hypersensitivity.
explanation: Allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, is strongly associated with HLA-B*58:01, which is common in several Asian populations. Carriers should receive an alternative such as febuxostat. Starting at a low dose also lowers risk.
pearl: HLA-B*15:02 is the corresponding risk allele for carbamazepine.

subject: medicine
stem: A patient has pulmonary tuberculosis resistant to rifampicin and isoniazid but susceptible to fluoroquinolones. Which regimen does WHO now prefer?
options: 6 months of bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid and moxifloxacin
18 to 20 months of an injectable-based regimen
reason: BPaLM for 6 months is the preferred all-oral regimen.
explanation: The TB-PRACTECAL trial showed that 6 months of bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid and moxifloxacin was at least as effective as longer standard regimens, with fewer adverse events. If fluoroquinolone resistance is present, moxifloxacin is dropped and BPaL is used.
pearl: Monitor for linezolid toxicity: neuropathy, optic neuritis and myelosuppression.

subject: surgery
stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the six predictors in the Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI)?
reason: Age is not an RCRI variable.
explanation: The RCRI uses six predictors: high-risk surgery (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic or suprainguinal vascular), ischaemic heart disease, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, insulin-treated diabetes and creatinine above 2 mg/dL. Risk of major cardiac events rises with the number present.
pearl: Three or more RCRI predictors mark high cardiac risk.

subject: surgery
stem: A 66-year-old needs an elevated-risk abdominal operation. He climbs two flights of stairs daily without symptoms and has no active cardiac condition. What is the next step?
options: Proceed to surgery without further cardiac testing
reason: Functional capacity of 4 METs or more without symptoms: proceed.
explanation: In the stepwise ACC/AHA approach, patients with elevated risk but good functional capacity (4 METs or more, such as climbing two flights of stairs) go to surgery without further testing. Testing is reserved for poor or unknown capacity, and only if the result would change management.
pearl: A Duke Activity Status Index score above 34 roughly equals 4 METs.

subject: surgery
stem: After elective PCI with a drug-eluting stent for stable coronary disease, elective noncardiac surgery should ideally be delayed for at least:
reason: About 6 months after a DES for chronic coronary disease.
explanation: Premature interruption of dual antiplatelet therapy after stenting risks stent thrombosis. Elective surgery is ideally deferred 6 months after a drug-eluting stent placed for stable disease, and 12 months after an acute coronary syndrome. After bare-metal stents, 30 days is the minimum.
pearl: If delay is harmful, surgery may be considered from 3 months, continuing aspirin.

subject: surgery
stem: A STOP-BANG score in which range indicates a high probability of moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea?
reason: STOP-BANG 5 to 8 = high risk of moderate to severe OSA.
explanation: STOP-BANG scores Snoring, Tiredness, Observed apnoea, high blood Pressure, BMI above 35, Age above 50, Neck circumference above 40 cm and male Gender. A score of 0 to 2 is low risk, 3 to 4 intermediate and 5 to 8 high risk.
pearl: Untreated OSA raises the risk of difficult airway, desaturation and postoperative opioid complications.

subject: surgery
stem: For smoking cessation to reduce postoperative wound and pulmonary complications, it should begin at least how long before surgery?
reason: At least 4 weeks of abstinence reduces complications.
explanation: Stopping 4 or more weeks before surgery reduces wound and respiratory complications, and longer abstinence gives greater benefit. Even 12 to 24 hours of abstinence lowers carboxyhaemoglobin, but that is not enough to reduce complications.
pearl: Nicotine replacement does not impair wound healing the way smoking does.

subject: surgery
stem: Which scoring system is used to stratify the risk of venous thromboembolism in general surgical patients?
reason: Caprini stratifies surgical VTE risk and guides prophylaxis.
explanation: The Caprini score adds weighted points for age, surgery type, malignancy, previous VTE, thrombophilia, immobility and other factors to guide mechanical and pharmacological prophylaxis. ARISCAT predicts pulmonary complications, Goldman cardiac risk, and Charlson overall comorbidity.
pearl: Caprini 5 or more is highest risk; consider extended prophylaxis after major cancer surgery.

subject: surgery
stem: Which of the following is a predictor in the ARISCAT score for postoperative pulmonary complications?
options: Preoperative SpO2 below 91% on room air
reason: Low preoperative SpO2 is an ARISCAT variable.
explanation: ARISCAT includes age, preoperative SpO2, respiratory infection in the last month, preoperative anaemia (Hb 10 g/dL or less), upper abdominal or intrathoracic incision, operation longer than 2 hours, and emergency surgery. Obesity and sex are not part of it.
pearl: Upper abdominal and thoracic incisions carry the biggest weight after low SpO2.

subject: surgery
stem: In the POISE trial, starting high-dose extended-release metoprolol on the day of noncardiac surgery:
options: Had no effect on any cardiac outcome
Reduced stroke without affecting myocardial infarction
Reduced myocardial infarction but increased stroke and death
reason: Fewer MIs, but more strokes, hypotension and deaths.
explanation: POISE showed that beta blockers started acutely before surgery lowered myocardial infarction but increased stroke and total mortality, largely through hypotension and bradycardia. Patients already taking beta blockers should continue them; starting them on the day of surgery is avoided.
pearl: If started, begin days to weeks ahead and titrate to heart rate and blood pressure.

subject: surgery
stem: A patient with atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 4), no prior stroke, on warfarin is scheduled for elective colectomy. What is the best plan?
options: Stop warfarin 5 days before surgery without heparin bridging
Stop warfarin and bridge with therapeutic LMWH
reason: BRIDGE trial: bridging adds bleeding without preventing thromboembolism.
explanation: In the BRIDGE trial of AF patients interrupting warfarin, no bridging was non-inferior for arterial thromboembolism and caused less major bleeding than LMWH bridging. Warfarin is stopped about 5 days before surgery and restarted once haemostasis is secure.
pearl: Bridging is still considered for mechanical mitral valves or stroke or VTE within 3 months.

subject: surgery
stem: Before elective surgery, an SGLT2 inhibitor such as empagliflozin should be stopped how long beforehand?
reason: Stop 3 days before (4 for ertugliflozin) to avoid euglycaemic DKA.
explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose during fasting and surgical stress. Canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are stopped at least 3 days before scheduled surgery, ertugliflozin at least 4 days, and restarted once eating normally.
pearl: Check ketones, not just glucose, if a patient on an SGLT2 inhibitor becomes acidotic.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy with controlled entry into the biliary tract and no spillage is classified as which wound class?
reason: Controlled entry into a hollow viscus = clean-contaminated.
explanation: Class I wounds do not enter the respiratory, alimentary, genital or urinary tract. Class II enter them under controlled conditions without unusual contamination. Class III includes gross spillage, major breaks in sterile technique and fresh trauma. Class IV involves pus or perforated viscus.
pearl: Wound class is one of the components of the NNIS SSI risk index.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: When vancomycin is used for surgical prophylaxis, the infusion should begin:
reason: Vancomycin needs a longer infusion, so start it within 2 hours of incision.
explanation: Most prophylactic agents such as cefazolin are given within 60 minutes before incision so tissue levels peak at incision. Vancomycin and fluoroquinolones need longer infusions and are started within 120 minutes. Giving it too late or too early both increase SSI.
pearl: Infuse vancomycin over at least an hour to avoid red man syndrome.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: During a long operation, cefazolin prophylaxis should be redosed every:
reason: Cefazolin is redosed every 4 hours of surgery.
explanation: Redosing keeps tissue levels above the MIC throughout the operation. The interval is about two half-lives of the drug, which is 4 hours for cefazolin. A dose is also repeated after blood loss of more than 1,500 mL.
pearl: Cefazolin is dosed at 2 g, and 3 g for patients weighing 120 kg or more.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: A patient with a permanent pacemaker needs a laparotomy. Which precaution with electrosurgery is correct?
options: No precautions are needed with modern devices
Use bipolar where possible and keep the current path away from the device
Increase monopolar power to shorten activation time
Place the return electrode over the pulse generator
reason: Minimise monopolar use and keep its current path away from the device.
explanation: Monopolar current can be sensed as cardiac activity, causing inhibition, or can reset the device. Bipolar diathermy is preferred, monopolar bursts kept short, and the return pad placed so the current path does not cross the generator or leads. Pacemaker-dependent patients may need asynchronous reprogramming or a magnet.
pearl: Check and reprogramme cardiac devices after surgery if they were altered.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: With modern isolated electrosurgical generators, the most common cause of a patient burn at the dispersive electrode is:
options: Poor contact of the return electrode pad
reason: Partial pad contact concentrates current and burns the skin.
explanation: If the dispersive pad loses contact, current density at the remaining area rises and causes a burn. Return electrode monitoring systems measure pad impedance and stop the generator if contact is poor. Isolated generators largely eliminate alternate-site burns through ECG leads.
pearl: Place the pad over well-vascularised muscle, away from bony prominences and metal implants.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: Which laparoscopic port arrangement carries the highest risk of capacitive coupling injury?
options: Low-voltage cut waveform through a plastic port
Metal cannula held by a plastic anchoring collar
reason: Hybrid (metal-plastic) cannulas trap the induced charge.
explanation: A capacitor forms when an insulator separates two conductors. With an all-metal port, induced current disperses through the abdominal wall. A plastic collar insulates the metal cannula, so charge can discharge into adjacent bowel. High-voltage coagulation current increases the risk.
pearl: Insulation failure and direct coupling are the other two mechanisms of stray energy injury.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: During tracheostomy, which step most reduces the risk of an operating room fire?
options: Lower inspired oxygen to 30% or less before using diathermy near the airway
Increase oxygen flow to clear the field
Use monopolar diathermy to open the trachea
Use alcohol-based prep and drape immediately
reason: Remove the oxidiser part of the fire triad.
explanation: Fire needs an ignition source, fuel and an oxidiser. In airway surgery, oxygen enrichment near the field is the main modifiable factor, so FiO2 is reduced to the minimum needed. Alcohol preps must be allowed to dry, and the trachea is opened with a scalpel, not diathermy.
pearl: Pooled alcohol prep under drapes is a classic fuel source.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: Pneumoperitoneum with CO2 at 15 mmHg most typically causes:
options: Reduced venous return and raised systemic vascular resistance
reason: Raised intra-abdominal pressure compresses the IVC and raises afterload.
explanation: Insufflation reduces venous return and increases systemic vascular resistance, while CO2 absorption raises PaCO2. Splinting of the diaphragm reduces functional residual capacity and compliance, and renal blood flow and urine output fall.
pearl: Head-down tilt worsens ventilation; head-up tilt worsens venous return.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: According to the STITCH trial, closing a midline laparotomy with the small-bites technique means:
options: Bites 5 mm from the wound edge, placed 5 mm apart
Bites 1 cm from the edge, placed 1 cm apart
A suture to wound length ratio of 2:1
reason: 5 mm by 5 mm bites reduced incisional hernia.
explanation: The STITCH trial showed that small bites in the aponeurosis, 5 mm from the edge and 5 mm apart with a slowly absorbable suture, reduced incisional hernia at 1 year compared with large bites. A suture to wound length ratio of at least 4:1 is maintained.
pearl: Prophylactic mesh is also considered in high-risk midline laparotomies.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 19 · Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
topic: Principles of Preoperative and Operative Surgery
stem: Intraoperative hypothermia below 36 °C is associated with:
options: Increased surgical site infection and blood loss
reason: Hypothermia impairs immunity and coagulation.
explanation: Mild hypothermia causes vasoconstriction and reduced tissue oxygen, impairs neutrophil function, and slows clotting enzymes. It increases wound infection, blood loss, transfusion and cardiac events, and prolongs drug action. Active warming keeps core temperature at 36 °C or more.
pearl: Most heat loss happens in the first hour after induction from redistribution.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: What is the earliest sign of malignant hyperthermia under general anaesthesia?
reason: Rising end-tidal CO2 despite more ventilation comes first.
explanation: Malignant hyperthermia is triggered by volatile agents and succinylcholine in patients with RYR1 mutations. Uncontrolled calcium release causes hypermetabolism: rising end-tidal CO2, tachycardia and masseter rigidity first, with hyperthermia, hyperkalaemia and myoglobinuria later.
pearl: Treat with dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg, repeated as needed, and stop all triggers.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: In which patient is succinylcholine contraindicated because of the risk of hyperkalaemia?
options: Six hours after a major burn
Ten days after a major burn
Rapid sequence induction for a full stomach
reason: Extrajunctional receptors develop from about 24 to 48 hours after a burn.
explanation: Burns, denervation, crush injury and prolonged immobility cause upregulation of extrajunctional acetylcholine receptors. Succinylcholine then releases large amounts of potassium. The risk starts 24 to 48 hours after injury and lasts for months, so it is safe in the first hours after a burn.
pearl: Rocuronium with sugammadex available is the alternative for rapid sequence induction.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: A patient has seizures and then ventricular arrhythmia after a large-volume bupivacaine block. Besides airway management and CPR, what is the specific treatment?
options: Propofol infusion as a lipid source
reason: Lipid emulsion treats local anaesthetic systemic toxicity.
explanation: Lipid emulsion acts as a lipid sink and supports myocardial energy use. A bolus of 1.5 mL/kg of 20% emulsion is followed by an infusion. Adrenaline is used in reduced doses, and vasopressin, calcium channel blockers, beta blockers and further local anaesthetic are avoided.
pearl: Propofol is not a substitute: its lipid content is too low and it depresses the heart.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: The maximum recommended dose of lidocaine with adrenaline for infiltration is about:
reason: About 7 mg/kg with adrenaline, 4.5 mg/kg without.
explanation: Adrenaline causes local vasoconstriction, slowing absorption and allowing a higher safe dose. For bupivacaine the limits are about 2 mg/kg plain and 3 mg/kg with adrenaline. Toxicity starts with perioral numbness, tinnitus and agitation before seizures and cardiac effects.
pearl: Tumescent lidocaine in liposuction is a special case with much higher dosing.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: Sugammadex reverses neuromuscular blockade caused by:
reason: It encapsulates steroidal neuromuscular blockers.
explanation: Sugammadex is a modified cyclodextrin that binds rocuronium and vecuronium in a one-to-one complex. It can reverse even profound block, unlike neostigmine. It has no effect on benzylisoquinolinium agents such as atracurium or on succinylcholine.
pearl: It also binds progesterone and can reduce hormonal contraceptive effect for 7 days.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: A patient with poorly controlled diabetes and a BMI of 42 kg/m2, but no other disease, would be classified as:
reason: Morbid obesity (BMI 40 or more) or poorly controlled diabetes = ASA III.
explanation: ASA III means severe systemic disease with substantive functional limitation, including poorly controlled diabetes or hypertension and BMI of 40 or more. ASA II is mild disease such as well-controlled diabetes or BMI 30 to 40. ASA IV is severe disease that is a constant threat to life.
pearl: Adding E denotes emergency surgery.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: A patient has a severe postural headache 3 days after spinal anaesthesia that has not settled with fluids, caffeine and analgesics. What is the definitive treatment?
reason: Epidural blood patch seals the dural leak.
explanation: Post-dural puncture headache is worse when upright and eases lying down, from CSF leak and intracranial hypotension. Most resolve with conservative care. An epidural blood patch of about 20 mL of autologous blood relieves symptoms in most patients when conservative care fails.
pearl: Smaller-gauge pencil-point needles reduce the incidence.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: In a transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block, local anaesthetic is deposited between which layers?
options: Rectus abdominis and posterior rectus sheath
reason: The anterior rami of T6 to L1 run between internal oblique and transversus.
explanation: The thoracolumbar nerves supplying the anterior abdominal wall travel in the plane between internal oblique and transversus abdominis. A TAP block gives somatic analgesia of the wall but no visceral analgesia, so it is part of multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia.
pearl: The rectus sheath block lies between rectus and posterior sheath and suits midline wounds.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: A patient on a prolonged high-dose propofol infusion in ICU develops metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia and heart failure. What is the diagnosis?
reason: Propofol infusion syndrome impairs mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation.
explanation: The syndrome is linked to doses above about 4 mg/kg per hour for more than 48 hours, especially with catecholamines and steroids. Features are lactic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia, lipaemia, arrhythmia and cardiac failure. Stopping propofol is the key step.
pearl: Rising lactate and triglycerides are early warnings.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 20 · Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
topic: Anesthesiology Principles, Pain Management, and Sedation
stem: Glycopyrrolate is given with neostigmine during reversal of neuromuscular blockade to prevent:
reason: It blocks the muscarinic effects of raised acetylcholine.
explanation: Neostigmine inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine at nicotinic and muscarinic receptors. Unopposed muscarinic effects cause bradycardia, secretions and bronchospasm. Glycopyrrolate, an antimuscarinic that does not cross the blood-brain barrier, is paired with it.
pearl: Neostigmine has a ceiling effect and cannot reverse profound block.

subject: surgery
stem: Under ERAS and current anaesthetic guidance, an adult without delayed gastric emptying may drink clear fluids up to how long before induction?
reason: Clear fluids up to 2 hours, solids up to 6 hours.
explanation: Prolonged fasting increases thirst, anxiety, dehydration and insulin resistance without reducing aspiration risk. Clear fluids are allowed up to 2 hours and a light meal up to 6 hours before anaesthesia in patients without gastroparesis or obstruction.
pearl: Diabetics with gastroparesis and patients with bowel obstruction are exceptions.

subject: surgery
stem: What is the main purpose of a preoperative carbohydrate drink in ERAS protocols?
reason: Carbohydrate loading puts patients in a fed metabolic state.
explanation: A clear carbohydrate drink the evening before and 2 to 3 hours before surgery attenuates the postoperative insulin resistance caused by surgical stress. It also improves thirst and wellbeing, and helps preserve muscle mass.
pearl: Its use in insulin-treated diabetics remains debated.

subject: surgery
stem: For elective colorectal resection, which bowel preparation strategy is associated with lower surgical site infection and anastomotic leak?
options: Mechanical preparation combined with oral antibiotics
reason: Mechanical preparation alone gives no benefit; oral antibiotics add it.
explanation: Large database studies and several trials show that mechanical preparation alone does not reduce complications, while adding oral non-absorbable antibiotics lowers SSI and leak. Many centres now use combined preparation for left-sided and rectal resections.
pearl: IV prophylactic antibiotics at induction are still given.

subject: surgery
stem: After elective colectomy within an ERAS pathway, routine nasogastric decompression should be:
reason: Routine NG tubes increase complications without benefit.
explanation: Meta-analyses show that routine nasogastric decompression increases fever, atelectasis and pneumonia and delays return of bowel function. Tubes placed during surgery are removed before reversal of anaesthesia, and used later only for vomiting or established ileus.
pearl: Early oral intake does not increase leak rates.

subject: surgery
stem: The RELIEF trial compared restrictive with moderately liberal intravenous fluids in major abdominal surgery. What did it show?
options: The restrictive regimen improved disability-free survival
The restrictive regimen increased acute kidney injury
The liberal regimen increased anastomotic leak
reason: Too restrictive raised AKI; aim for near-zero balance.
explanation: RELIEF found no difference in disability-free survival, but the restrictive arm had more acute kidney injury and surgical site infection. The message is to avoid both overload and excessive restriction, aiming for a modestly positive fluid balance of around 1 to 2 litres.
pearl: Stop intravenous fluids as soon as the patient drinks.

subject: surgery
stem: After elective colorectal resection in an ERAS pathway, oral intake should generally begin:
reason: Early feeding is safe and speeds recovery.
explanation: Oral fluids and diet within 24 hours do not increase anastomotic leak and are associated with faster return of bowel function and shorter stay. Waiting for flatus or bowel sounds has no physiological basis.
pearl: Oral nutritional supplements help patients who eat little.

subject: surgery
stem: Alvimopan shortens postoperative ileus by acting as:
reason: It blocks gut opioid receptors without reversing analgesia.
explanation: Alvimopan does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so it blocks opioid effects on the bowel while central analgesia remains. It is used after bowel resection and is restricted to short courses because of a cardiovascular signal with long-term use.
pearl: Chewing gum and minimising opioids also reduce ileus.

subject: surgery
stem: Within ERAS programmes, better outcomes are seen when overall protocol compliance exceeds about:
reason: High compliance (above about 70%) improves outcomes.
explanation: Data from colorectal ERAS programmes show a dose-response relationship: complications and length of stay fall as compliance with the protocol elements rises, with clear benefit above roughly 70%. Auditing compliance is a core ERAS activity.
pearl: No single element drives the benefit; the bundle does.

subject: surgery
stem: For analgesia after laparoscopic colorectal surgery in an ERAS pathway, which approach is preferred?
options: Multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia, with spinal or abdominal wall blocks
Patient-controlled morphine as the sole agent
reason: Epidurals add little after laparoscopy and can delay mobilisation.
explanation: Thoracic epidurals are recommended for open colorectal surgery. After laparoscopic surgery they can cause hypotension and delay recovery, so a multimodal regimen with paracetamol, NSAIDs, and spinal analgesia or TAP blocks is favoured to limit systemic opioids.
pearl: Opioid-sparing analgesia also reduces nausea and ileus.

subject: surgery
stem: Which is NOT one of the four Apfel risk factors for postoperative nausea and vomiting?
options: History of motion sickness or PONV
reason: Being a non-smoker is the risk factor; smoking is protective.
explanation: The Apfel score counts female sex, non-smoking status, history of PONV or motion sickness, and postoperative opioids. With 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 factors the risk is roughly 10, 20, 40, 60 and 80%. Prophylaxis is scaled to the number of factors.
pearl: Combining antiemetics from different classes gives additive benefit.

subject: surgery
stem: Which type of collagen predominates in early granulation tissue?
reason: Type III dominates early; type I in mature scar.
explanation: In the proliferative phase, fibroblasts lay down type III collagen first. During remodelling it is replaced by type I collagen, with increasing cross-linking. Normal skin has a type I to type III ratio of about 4:1.
pearl: Type IV collagen is found in basement membranes.

subject: surgery
stem: What is the maximum tensile strength a healed skin wound eventually reaches, compared with unwounded skin?
reason: A scar never regains full strength; it plateaus around 80%.
explanation: Tensile strength is about 20% at 3 weeks and rises over months during remodelling as collagen cross-links and reorganises. It reaches a maximum of roughly 80% of unwounded skin and never fully recovers.
pearl: Fascia regains strength slowly, which is why incisional hernias appear late.

subject: surgery
stem: Scurvy impairs wound healing mainly because vitamin C is needed for:
options: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine in procollagen
reason: Without hydroxylation, collagen triple helices are unstable.
explanation: Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases need ascorbate as a cofactor. Underhydroxylated collagen cannot form stable triple helices or cross-link, so wounds fail to gain strength and old scars can break down.
pearl: Iron and oxygen are the other cofactors of these hydroxylases.

subject: surgery
stem: Which feature best distinguishes a keloid from a hypertrophic scar?
options: It is raised above the skin
It appears within weeks of injury
It extends beyond the borders of the original wound
reason: Keloids invade beyond the wound edge; hypertrophic scars do not.
explanation: Hypertrophic scars stay within the wound, appear early and often regress, especially when tension is relieved. Keloids extend beyond the original margins, rarely regress and recur often after excision. Both are raised and may itch.
pearl: Keloids are common in darker skin and on the earlobe, sternum and shoulders.

subject: surgery
stem: Which agent can partly reverse the inhibitory effect of corticosteroids on wound healing?
reason: Vitamin A counteracts steroid inhibition of inflammation and collagen.
explanation: Steroids suppress the inflammatory phase, fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis. Vitamin A, given orally or topically, restores the inflammatory response and partly reverses the impairment, although it does not reverse effects on infection risk.
pearl: Steroid effects are most marked when given in the first days after wounding.

subject: surgery
stem: Which cell is chiefly responsible for wound contraction?
reason: Myofibroblasts contain smooth muscle actin and pull wound edges together.
explanation: Myofibroblasts are specialised fibroblasts expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin. They appear in granulation tissue and contract the wound, reducing its size. Excessive contraction across joints causes contractures.
pearl: Full-thickness grafts limit contraction better than split-thickness grafts.

subject: surgery
stem: From about 48 to 96 hours after injury, which cell becomes the predominant and essential cell in the wound?
reason: Macrophages direct the transition to repair.
explanation: Neutrophils dominate in the first 24 to 48 hours. Macrophages then predominate, clearing debris and releasing growth factors such as TGF-beta and PDGF that recruit fibroblasts and drive angiogenesis. Healing can proceed without neutrophils but not without macrophages.
pearl: Lymphocytes appear later, around day 5 to 7.

subject: surgery
stem: A man has a non-healing ulcer in an old burn scar on his leg. Biopsy is most likely to show:
reason: Marjolin ulcer is a squamous cell carcinoma in a chronic wound.
explanation: Malignant change in chronic scars, burns, sinuses or venous ulcers is usually squamous cell carcinoma and appears after a long latency. It is often aggressive, with a higher rate of nodal spread than ordinary skin SCC. Any chronic ulcer that changes should be biopsied.
pearl: Treatment is wide excision; assess regional nodes.

subject: surgery
stem: Which growth factor is approved as a topical treatment for diabetic foot ulcers?
reason: Becaplermin is recombinant platelet-derived growth factor.
explanation: Becaplermin gel improves healing of neuropathic diabetic foot ulcers when combined with offloading and debridement. PDGF attracts and stimulates fibroblasts and macrophages. Its use has been tempered by concern about malignancy with prolonged use.
pearl: Offloading and adequate perfusion matter more than any topical agent.

subject: surgery
stem: Negative pressure wound therapy is most commonly applied at a continuous pressure of:
reason: The standard setting is about -125 mmHg.
explanation: Negative pressure removes exudate, reduces oedema, draws wound edges together and stimulates granulation through mechanical stress on cells. Around -125 mmHg continuous is standard. Lower settings are used over fragile tissue or near exposed vessels.
pearl: Never place the foam directly on exposed vessels or bowel without a protective layer.

subject: surgery
stem: A patient develops a pelvic abscess 10 days after anterior resection. Under CDC definitions this is:
reason: Infection in a cavity or organ opened at surgery = organ/space SSI.
explanation: Superficial incisional SSI involves skin and subcutaneous tissue. Deep incisional SSI involves fascia and muscle. Organ/space SSI involves any part of the anatomy opened or manipulated during the operation, such as an intra-abdominal or pelvic abscess.
pearl: Surveillance usually runs for 30 days, or 90 days for certain procedures.

subject: surgery
stem: The most common organism causing SSI after clean surgery is:
reason: Skin flora, mainly S. aureus, cause clean-wound SSI.
explanation: In clean procedures the source is usually the patient's own skin flora, especially Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci. In clean-contaminated and contaminated bowel surgery, gram-negative enteric bacteria and anaerobes become important.
pearl: Prophylaxis choice follows the expected flora of the site.

subject: surgery
stem: If hair must be removed from the operative site, it should be:
options: Removed with depilatory cream a week before
Shaved with a razor the night before
Shaved with a razor in theatre
reason: Razors cause microabrasions that colonise.
explanation: Shaving creates small skin cuts that become colonised, increasing SSI, particularly when done the night before. Hair is removed only if it interferes with surgery, using clippers just before the operation.
pearl: Not removing hair at all is equally acceptable.

subject: surgery
stem: For skin antisepsis in clean-contaminated surgery, which preparation reduced SSI compared with aqueous povidone-iodine in a landmark trial?
reason: Chlorhexidine-alcohol beat povidone-iodine (Darouiche, NEJM 2010).
explanation: Alcohol gives rapid killing and chlorhexidine adds a persistent residual effect. In the trial, chlorhexidine-alcohol lowered superficial and deep incisional SSI. Alcohol preps must dry fully before draping and diathermy to avoid fire.
pearl: Chlorhexidine is avoided on mucous membranes, the eye and the middle ear.

subject: surgery
stem: CDC guidance on perioperative glucose control for surgical patients, with or without diabetes, recommends keeping blood glucose below:
reason: Target below 200 mg/dL to reduce SSI.
explanation: Hyperglycaemia impairs neutrophil function and raises SSI risk. The 2017 CDC guideline recommends perioperative glucose below 200 mg/dL in all patients. Very tight targets risk hypoglycaemia without additional SSI benefit.
pearl: HbA1c reflects chronic control; perioperative glucose drives acute risk.

subject: surgery
stem: After a clean procedure such as inguinal hernia repair with mesh, prophylactic antibiotics should:
options: Continue until the drain is removed
Not be continued after the incision is closed
reason: Additional doses after closure do not reduce SSI.
explanation: CDC and WHO guidance recommends against extending prophylaxis after wound closure, even when drains are present. Extended courses add resistance, Clostridioides difficile infection and cost without benefit.
pearl: Therapeutic antibiotics for established infection are a separate decision.

subject: surgery
stem: Which measure reduces SSI in known nasal carriers of Staphylococcus aureus undergoing cardiothoracic or orthopaedic surgery?
options: Intranasal mupirocin with chlorhexidine body wash
reason: Decolonisation lowers S. aureus SSI in carriers.
explanation: Screening and decolonising carriers with nasal mupirocin and chlorhexidine washing for about 5 days reduces S. aureus infections, especially after cardiac and orthopaedic implant surgery.
pearl: MRSA carriers may also need vancomycin added to prophylaxis.

subject: surgery
stem: Which is NOT a component of the NNIS SSI risk index?
options: Operation longer than the 75th percentile for that procedure
reason: NNIS uses ASA, wound class and duration only.
explanation: The NNIS index gives one point each for ASA 3 or more, contaminated or dirty wound, and duration beyond the 75th percentile for that procedure. Laparoscopic approach lowers the score by one for some procedures.
pearl: It is used to compare SSI rates between hospitals fairly.

subject: surgery
stem: A patient has a red, tender, discharging superficial incisional SSI 6 days after laparotomy, without systemic signs. What is the main treatment?
options: Open the wound to drain it
reason: Drainage is the key treatment for incisional SSI.
explanation: Superficial SSI is treated by removing sutures or staples, opening and draining the collection and packing or applying negative pressure. Antibiotics are added for spreading cellulitis, systemic signs or immunosuppression. Fascial integrity should be checked.
pearl: Send pus for culture to guide any antibiotics.

subject: surgery
stem: WHO guidance recommends which suture material to reduce SSI, regardless of wound class?
reason: Triclosan-coated sutures reduce SSI.
explanation: Triclosan is an antibacterial agent that inhibits colonisation of the suture. Meta-analyses showed reduced SSI across wound classes, and WHO gives a conditional recommendation for its use.
pearl: Multifilament sutures harbour bacteria more than monofilament.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: A postoperative complication that needs reoperation under general anaesthesia is graded under Clavien-Dindo as:
reason: Intervention under general anaesthesia = IIIb.
explanation: Grade I needs no specific treatment beyond simple measures. Grade II needs drugs, transfusion or parenteral nutrition. Grade III needs surgical, endoscopic or radiological intervention: IIIa without and IIIb with general anaesthesia. Grade IV is life-threatening with organ failure needing ICU. Grade V is death.
pearl: The suffix 'd' marks a complication that persists at discharge.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: A patient needs a blood transfusion for postoperative anaemia. Under Clavien-Dindo this is:
reason: Transfusion counts as grade II.
explanation: Grade II includes complications needing pharmacological treatment beyond the allowed simple drugs (antiemetics, antipyretics, analgesics, diuretics, electrolytes), as well as blood transfusion and total parenteral nutrition.
pearl: Wound infections opened at the bedside remain grade I.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: Under Clavien-Dindo, acute kidney injury requiring dialysis in ICU is graded as:
reason: Single-organ dysfunction needing ICU = IVa.
explanation: Grade IV covers life-threatening complications needing intensive care: IVa is single-organ dysfunction, including dialysis, and IVb is multi-organ dysfunction. Brain haemorrhage and ischaemic stroke count as grade IV, but TIA does not.
pearl: Grade V is death of the patient.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: What does the Comprehensive Complication Index (CCI) add to the Clavien-Dindo classification?
options: It measures complications after discharge only
It sums all complications into a single 0 to 100 score
It grades only the most severe complication
reason: CCI integrates every complication, not just the worst.
explanation: Clavien-Dindo reports the single most severe complication. The CCI weights each complication by its grade and combines them into a continuous score from 0 (no complications) to 100 (death), giving a more sensitive measure of total morbidity.
pearl: CCI is increasingly used as an outcome measure in surgical trials.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: In surgical quality research, failure to rescue is defined as:
options: Failure to complete the planned operation
reason: Failure to rescue = mortality among patients with a major complication.
explanation: Hospitals with high and low mortality often have similar complication rates. The difference lies mainly in failure to rescue: how well complications are recognised and managed. Staffing, ICU access and escalation pathways drive it.
pearl: Early warning scores and rapid response teams target failure to rescue.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: Abdominal compartment syndrome is defined as sustained intra-abdominal pressure above:
reason: IAP above 20 mmHg with new organ dysfunction.
explanation: Intra-abdominal hypertension is a sustained pressure of 12 mmHg or more, graded I to IV. Abdominal compartment syndrome is sustained pressure above 20 mmHg with new organ dysfunction or failure. Bladder pressure is the standard measurement.
pearl: Decompressive laparotomy is the definitive treatment when medical measures fail.

subject: surgery
chapter: Ch 26 · Surgical Complications: Overview and Grading
stem: Which finding is the classic warning sign of impending fascial dehiscence after laparotomy?
options: Mild erythema at the suture line
reason: Pink serous fluid from the wound signals fascial separation.
